verdict.rationale: mise's docs say that once you activate it in your shell, entering a project puts its tool versions on PATH and loads its env vars (from mise.toml, .env files and secrets), and leaving restores the environment. Activation updates tools and env vars as the shell changes directories, nested configs override parent ones, and a shims mode covers editors and scripts. Community users describe it as a direnv/asdf replacement for per-project environments. Missing for 10: independent hands-on reports that specifically confirm the automatic switch on entering and leaving a directory, as opposed to general praise of mise as an environment manager.
